title: Alibaba may lower data centre target amid major shifts in global computing policy
text:
Alibaba may lower data centre target amid major shifts in global computing policy | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Published / 20 Nov 2026 10:13 S M L XL Alibaba may lower data centre target amid major shifts in global computing policy
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 Preliminary assessments indicate that Chinese technology giant Alibaba may lower its previously announced target of more than 20GW of global data centre capacity by 2032, with capital expenditure potentially reduced to some extent. （Reuters） Chinese technology giant Alibaba may lower its long-term target of building 20 gigawatts (GW) of data centre capacity, with a corresponding reduction in overall capital expenditure, citing significant uncertainty in global supply chains and major shifts in policies governing computing capacity. 
 According to reports by Lanjing News, Radio Television Hong Kong and other outlets, Alibaba Group chief executive Eddie Wu told a second-quarter earnings call on Thursday (19 November) that major changes in computing capacity policies across regions worldwide would affect Alibaba Cloud’s data centre construction. 
 Wu said preliminary assessments indicated that Alibaba might lower its previously announced target of more than 20GW of global data centre capacity by 2032, with capital expenditure potentially reduced to some extent. 
 However, the company’s management believes the impact of new US Department of Commerce rules governing computing capacity on the development of artificial intelligence (AI) products will be temporary. The company is already using its self-developed chips to train its next generation of large AI models. 
 Wu said global demand for AI computing capacity still outstripped supply, a situation that would not change in the next few years. Infrastructure built on self-developed domestic computing technology would underpin the group’s AI revenue growth. He said the company was maintaining its targets for the cloud business to achieve US$100 billion (S$129.1 billion) in external revenue and a profit margin of more than 20% by 2030. 
 Alibaba’s management expects computing capacity shortages in China to be most acute in 2027 and 2028, when the group’s current round of investment in computing capacity will also peak. As the domestic computing supply chain expands, the group expects to turn cash-flow positive in the second half of 2028.
